# Leaf Area Index: How Much Leaf Is Standing Over the Ground

Leaf area index is the total one-sided area of leaves in a patch of ground, divided by the ground area under them. A value of 3 means there are three square metres of leaf for every square metre of soil. Simple enough. The part I liked was the numbers: 0 for bare soil, around 6 or 7 for a dense forest canopy. I wanted to check whether I understood it or only liked them.

What I think it means: leaves do the catching of light, so LAI roughly tells you how much light gets intercepted, and how much water and carbon the plants can move. Two stands with the same height can differ a lot in LAI, because a sparse crop and a closed forest look different from above but are not the same thing underneath.

What I am guessing: that satellites estimate LAI from how much red light is absorbed and how much near-infrared is reflected, and that this is an indirect measure. I have not seen the equations, so I am taking the indirect part on trust. Also I am not sure whether LAI counts only one side of each leaf, which the definition says it does, or whether people sometimes quote projected area instead. Those would give different numbers for the same canopy.

So: I understood the definition. The use is clearer now. The measurement is still a guess I should check.
